audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat operating liquidity as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Operating-cash requirement unquantified; $340.69 million is added to the bridge, equal to $13.19 per diluted share and 34.9% of the $977.0 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for working capital or settlement liquidity must be excluded from the equity bridge rather than added as distributable excess cash
audit_findings.evidence: We have historically used and expect to use in the future those funds to meet our capital requirements, which consist primarily of working capital for operational needs, capital expenditures for computer equipment and software used in our business, repurchases of common stock for treasury, dividend payments, and as opportunities arise, possible acquisitions of new businesses.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that cash and investments fund operating requirements, but it does not establish the minimum amount required. This is not yet a demonstrated $340.69 million error; however, the bridge addition is large enough that even a partial reclassification could materially reduce intrinsic value and the buy-below price.
audit_findings.action: Estimate minimum operating cash from monthly or quarterly receivables, inventory, payables, customer deposits, and settlement needs; rerun all scenarios with only demonstrably excess cash in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Supplier financing is obscured by the zero-debt bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $65.657 million at June 30, 2026, equal to $2.54 per diluted share and 6.7% of the $977.0 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Supplier-finance obligations enter normalized working capital through accounts payable; an unsupported or omitted funding benefit would make bridge cash appear more distributable than it is
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s outstanding payment obligations under the supplier finance programs, which are included in accounts payable on the consolidated balance sheets, were $ 58,563 and $ 47,763 at December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing resolves the missing-balance question and shows $65.657 million within accounts payable, with ordinary 30-to-50-day terms. Its classification outside debt is not itself an error. The unresolved issue is whether normalized working capital fully captures this financing and whether an unwind would consume cash; the record does not establish that an adjustment is required.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $65.657 million balance to normalized accounts payable and working-capital calculations, review concentration and termination terms, and rerun the bridge for any amount that must be repaid without replacement.

audit_findings.title: Nonoperating gains may remain in OE while investment assets are added separately
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.776 million pre-tax combined: $1.700 million in 2024 and $0.076 million in 2025; respectively 2.9% of 2024 OE and 0.1% of 2025 OE
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the gains raise historical OE and its trend while the associated investment assets are separately added in the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: Other income for the year ended December 31, 2025 was $0.1 million as a result of a realized gain on sale of short-term investments, compared to $1.7 million for the same period in the prior year as a result of a legal settlement received.
audit_findings.explanation: Inclusion has not been demonstrated, but the filed amounts are small relative to the affected OE observations and the $45.3 million anchor. The 2025 investment gain is negligible, and the one-time 2024 settlement is only 2.9% of that year's OE, so these items are not reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace other income through the 2024 and 2025 OE reconciliations and remove the $1.700 million settlement and $0.076 million investment gain if included; document the result without changing other inputs.

audit_findings.title: Cloud implementation spending can fall outside conventional capex
audit_findings.magnitude: Exact omitted spending unquantified; filed 2025 balances were $7.925 million gross, $7.146 million net, and $0.779 million of amortization
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash implementation additions should reduce OE as required reinvestment, either directly or through relevant operating-asset changes, while amortization must not be deducted twice
audit_findings.evidence: Costs incurred in implementing a cloud computing arrangement are deferred during the application development stage and presented within prepaid expenses and other current assets or other assets, as applicable, on the consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that material cloud implementation costs are capitalized outside property and equipment, but the supplied record does not show whether the OE calculation already captures their cash additions through prepaid and other-asset changes. The balance is meaningful relative to the $45.3 million anchor, but neither the recurring annual requirement nor the omitted amount is established.
audit_findings.action: Build a year-by-year rollforward of cloud implementation assets showing additions, amortization, and disposals; map each cash addition and amortization charge to the OE reconciliation and rerun only for net omissions.

audit_findings.title: Repeated severance should not receive a one-off add-back
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.115 million pre-tax for 2023-2025, including $6.013 million in 2025; a further $3.060 million was filed for the first half of 2026. The 2025 amount equals 13.3% of the $45.3 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Improper severance add-backs raise historical OE and therefore the log-trend anchor and projected operating value
audit_findings.evidence: In connection with these initiatives, we incurred severance expenses and other charges of $6.0 million, $0.4 million, and $2.7 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Recurring severance is demonstrated across 2023-2026, but the record does not demonstrate that the valuation actually added it back. If it did, the $6.013 million 2025 amount alone is large relative to the anchor and could materially overstate operating value, so this remains a material conditional error rather than a proven valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Inspect every OE reconciliation for 2023-2025 and any normalization feeding the anchor; reverse all severance add-backs, retain the expenses in OE, and rerun the trend and all valuation scenarios if any add-back occurred.
